players.product: NeoFuse OTP and PUF-based security IP

quarterly_data.signal: Company overview slide (Q2 2026 investor conference deck): 79M+ cumulative wafers shipped with eMemory IP, spanning 772 production processes from 0.5 um to 2 nm, and 5M wafers (8-inch-equivalent) shipped in 2026 H1. eMemory says it leads the global market in Logic NVM and PUF-based security IPs (company claim); 1370+ patents issued and 221 pending.
quarterly_data.figure: 79M+ cumulative wafers; 772 production processes; 5M wafers (8-inch-equivalent) shipped in 2026 H1

quarterly_data.signal: Accumulated advanced-node licensed tape-outs: 70 at leading-edge nodes (3nm-7nm) and 88 at mainstream advanced nodes (12nm/16nm); eMemory says it has over 150 advanced-node tape-out licenses, building a high-value royalty pipeline. Leading-edge tape-outs by application: HPC and data center 41, consumer electronics 20, automotive 5, industrial and robotics 3, others 1; by chip type: FPGA 21, CPU/GPU/DPU 11, SSD controller 8, retimer 4, ADAS 3, others 23. Mainstream advanced-node tape-outs by chip type: SoC 16, Ethernet IC 14, SSD controller 11, DDI 6, ASIC 5, others 36.

quarterly_data.signal: Business-development platforms (deck outlook): the PUF-based HSM Edge Server combines device identity, key and certificate management, secure OTA updates, signature verification, privacy protection and Post-Quantum Cryptography migration - early opportunities are progressing in automotive OTA, PKI and HSM integration, with potential to expand into industrial control, edge AI, smart devices, medical and data centers. For data centers and AI servers eMemory is upselling PUFrt from a hardware Root of Trust into a Caliptra-compatible Security Subsystem plus integration services; it is extending collaboration across CPU, AI accelerator and AI ASIC ecosystems, working with ecosystem partners on an end-to-end chiplet security framework, and strengthening its PUF-PQC portfolio with side-channel protection.
